content.evidence_note: Source-linked worked literature proof recipe. F.5's inner primitive and its F.1–F.4 dependencies are imported interfaces, not an independently proved local result. This Proof Method is not an additional Theorem or a complete standalone Algorithm record.
failure_modes: Using η_f at every outer stage introduces an unnecessary factor T in the fine statistical cost.
Returning a coarse point without the final accuracy conversion can omit C or fail true-gradient stationarity.
A radius-dependent noise overhead can multiply stochastic cost by log G, contradicting this worked accounting.
Per-inner-call truncations or uncharged multilevel samples do not establish the displayed fixed raw-call budget.
Similar bilevel or Moreau-envelope recipes with different oracle/output/expected-cost conventions are not automatically equivalent.
content.goal_pattern: Avoid paying final statistical accuracy at every outer stage while preserving true primal-gradient accuracy and a fixed raw-call guarantee.
content.key_choice: Use g_c(u,v)=f(u,v)+L||u−c||², P_c=Φ+L||u−c||², u_c*=argmin P_c, m(c)=2L(c−u_c*). Solve T coarse subproblems, then choose R uniformly independently of them and refine the SAME g_{x_R} from stored (x_{R+1},y_{R+1}) once.
content.key_relation: T=ceil(10^6LΔ/ε²), η_c=ε²/(10^6L), η_f=ε²/(10^6κL). Coarse statistical cost Tσ²/(μη_c)=O(κLΔσ²/ε⁴) up to constants in the nontrivial regime; the single fine cost σ²/(μη_f)=O(κ²σ²/ε²). Cold-start work adds √κ log(2+κ²G²/ε²+κ²LΔ/ε²), with the remaining multiplicative logarithms independent of G.
proof_skeleton: Theorem F.5 applies to g_c with ℓ=3L, α=L. Its gap controls primal suboptimality, giving EΦ(x_{t+1})+LE||x_{t+1}−x_t||²≤EΦ(x_t)−E||m(x_t)||²/(8L)+η_c. Telescope to bound average E||m(x_t)||²≤16ε²/10^6 and movement by Δ+Tη_c.

Use known initial energy O(G²/μ+κΔ). Strong monotonicity between subproblem saddles and the total movement estimate give later expected warm-start envelopes O(η_c+Δ+Tη_c), without extra G dependence. Fine refinement starts at expected energy O(η_c).

The final subproblem gap η_f yields E||∇P_{x_R}(xhat)||²≤8κLη_f and L||xhat−u*_{x_R}||≤||∇P_{x_R}(xhat)||. With ∇Φ(xhat)=m(x_R)+∇P_{x_R}(xhat)−2L(xhat−u*_{x_R}), the source obtains E||∇Φ(xhat)||²≤176ε²/10^6<ε²/12.

Sum coarse deterministic/statistical work as tilde O(A+B), one fine solve as tilde O(√κ+C), and the single explicit cold-start logarithm. In the nontrivial regime the additional √κ is absorbed by A. All random multilevel calls count as original oracle calls.

Let W be the known upper bound on expected TOTAL original calls. Couple the unrestricted run with execution capped at ceil(12W); output zero if the cap would be exceeded. Markov bounds truncation by 1/12 and the squared-gradient bound gives failure at most 1/12. The fixed-budget witness thus succeeds with probability at least 5/6, sufficient for the paper's 2/3 requirement.
content.required_inputs: The localized NC–SC model of Definitions 3.1–3.3: global joint L-smoothness, μ-strong concavity in unconstrained y, primal gap Δ, initial dual gradient residual at most G and only fresh conditionally unbiased joint gradients with joint variance ≤σ². Public parameter bounds must support tuning and known expected-work envelopes. Import Theorem F.5, including its random-subproblem/random-warm-start interface: expected Gap_g≤η from E[ℓ||u0−u*||²+μ||v0−v*||²]≤E0 at cost KΛ_g^8[√κ_g log(2+κ_gE0/η)+σ²/(μη)], α≥ℓ/4, κ_g=ℓ/μ, Λ_g=1+log(2+κ_g)+log(2+σ²/(μη)). No free exact inner solution is assumed.
transfer_obligations: Reestablish an inner expected saddle-gap primitive with the same actual oracle, unconditional random-start interface and additive initialization logarithm; a value-gap or joint-gradient theorem alone does not supply this interface.
Prove coarse descent, controlled movement and expected warm-start energies for the actual reduction, without passing unobserved radii as public algorithm inputs.
Prove the final certificate controls the true output gradient, including all condition-number factors; preserve C and pay it once.
Bound total ORIGINAL-call expectation by a known finite quantity, including random estimator work, before applying one global truncation. A fixed-budget conclusion needs this conversion.
Recheck public tuning, nontrivial regime, independent output-stage selection and conditional fresh-sampling assumptions under any transfer.

summary: A worked proof recipe separates T coarse solves, one fine solve and one cold-start logarithm, then converts total expected original calls into a fixed budget once.
title: Coarse proximal progress followed by one final statistical refinement
use_when: A proximal reduction permits coarse progress certificates while the final true-gradient output needs higher accuracy.
